title: Microsoft Teams: external presenters in event group chat
summary: The rollout, prerequisites and cross-tenant exposure match Microsoft's notice. Two external-access PowerShell calls need correction before publication: they omit required parameter values, and the tenant-level call also uses slash-separated alternatives that cannot be run as printed.

claims.claim: Event group chat is the private coordination chat for organisers, co-organisers and presenters in an event or structured meeting.
claims.quote: Event group chat, the private chat for organizers, co-organizers, and presenters in an event or structured meeting, will support external presenters.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to let presenters outside the hosting tenant participate in event group chat.
claims.quote: This change enables presenters who are outside the tenant hosting the meeting or event to participate in the event group chat.

claims.claim: The notice says the change stores no new customer data.

Does the change store new customer data?

- No. Expected changes on the client will only correct the tenantId to the external federated presenter's own tenant.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn describes the existing event group chat as available before, during and after an event.
claims.quote: The event group chat is available before, during, and after an event, and is a separate experience from the chat with attendees.

claims.claim: Event group chat is separate from attendee chat.

claims.quote: Event group chat (organizers, co-organizers, and presenters) | No control. | Can chat with presenters and co-organizers. Attendees don't use this chat during events.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the external-presenter event group chat change itself.

claims.claim: The described change is human chat participation, not an agent or automated action.
claims.quote: External presenters will be able to join the event group chat used for coordination during a meeting or event.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Tenant-level external organisation access is managed in Teams admin center under Users > External access.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to **Users** > **External access**.

claims.claim: Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration -AllowFederatedUsers / -AllowedDomains / -BlockedDomains is a PowerShell call that configures tenant external access.
claims.quote:
[-AllowedDomains <IAllowedDomainsChoice>]
    [-BlockedDomains <List>]
    [-BlockAllSubdomains <Boolean>]
    [-AllowFederatedUsers <Boolean>]
claims.fix: Replace the slash-separated parameter inventory with valid separate calls and explicit values or typed placeholders: 'Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration -AllowFederatedUsers $true'; 'Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration -AllowedDomains <allowed-domains-object>'; 'Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration -BlockedDomains <blocked-domains-list>'. Explain that these are alternatives for different operations, not one command, and that AllowedDomains requires an object created with New-CsEdgeAllowList or New-CsEdgeAllowAllKnownDomains. Cite the cmdlet reference for syntax and object construction; do not present '/' as PowerShell syntax. Update both front matter and the rendered table.

claims.claim: User external-access policies are managed in Teams admin center under Users > External access > Policies.
claims.quote:
In the Teams admin center, go to **Users** > **External access**.
2. Select the **Policies** tab.

claims.claim: Set-CsExternalAccessPolicy -EnableFederationAccess is a PowerShell call that changes a user's external-access policy.
claims.quote: [-EnableFederationAccess <Boolean>]
claims.fix: Supply the missing Boolean argument in both copies of the call, for example 'Set-CsExternalAccessPolicy -EnableFederationAccess $false' to disable federation in the default org-wide policy, as illustrated in manage-external-access. State the operation and policy target explicitly; use $true for enabling rather than implying the bare parameter is a switch.

claims.claim: The external-presenter event join-verification control is on Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to **Meetings** > **Events policies**.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalPresenterJoinVerification EOTP requires external-presenter verification for events created by organisers assigned the policy.
claims.quote:
To require external presenters to verify their identity before joining events created by organizers with this policy, run the following command:

```powershell
Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalPresenterJoinVerification EOTP

claims.where: controls[3].ui; controls[3].api; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No separate admin UI or API switch is documented for external presenters in event group chat.
claims.quote: Searched: "event group chat" admin disable PowerShell external presenters; "event group chat" "disable" "PowerShell". Opened plan-events, manage-event-chat and Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy; plan-events lists event group chat as 'No control'; no feature switch found.

claims.claim: External access generally requires both the organisation setting and the user policy to allow it.
claims.quote: For a user to use external access, both the organization setting and a user policy must allow it.

claims.claim: The organisation settings and user policies for external access are generally turned on by default.
claims.quote: Both the organization settings and user policies are turned on by default.

claims.claim: Organisation-level external-access settings can override user external-access policies.
claims.quote: Your organization's external access settings can override external access policies.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specifically confirmed how the existing user external-access policy applies to this new event group chat feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams "event group chat" "ExternalPresenterJoinVerification" policy external access; "event group chat" admin disable PowerShell external presenters. Read manage-external-access, manage-event-chat and MC1528011; no feature-specific user-policy mapping.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that event join verification also governs access to event group chat.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams "event group chat" "ExternalPresenterJoinVerification" policy external access. Opened events-external-presenter-join-verification and manage-event-chat; verification is documented for joining events, not for admitting presenters to group chat.

claims.claim: The Teams events planning page lists no admin control for the green room.
claims.quote: Searched: Green room and green room in the fetched plan-events page. Its Green room rows say 'No control' for admins and 'Can choose if green room is used for an event' for organisers.

claims.claim: The feature arrives for its intended users without a new feature-specific admin opt-in, subject to the existing green-room and external-collaboration prerequisites.
claims.quote: External presenters will be able to join the event group chat used for coordination during a meeting or event.

claims.claim: The notice uses External collaboration while the cited external-access article uses Users > External access, leaving the label difference unresolved.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to **Users** > **External access**.
claims.fix: Keep the path supported by the cited article, but replace 'the label difference is unresolved' with an explanation and citation to https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/unified-external-collab-settings-management-experience: Microsoft documents an External Collaboration section in the Teams admin center left rail which contains the existing External access page. Report both documented navigation descriptions rather than implying Microsoft has not explained their relationship.
